name: Morfessa

attributes.attribute: an Irish hero whose name means great wisdom
the wisdom master of Falias, one of the four capitals of the Tuatha De Danann
the great inauguration stone that came from Falias and was given to the Tuatha De by Morfessa

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Morfessa was an Irish hero. Her name means great wisdom. The magical race called the Tuatha De Danann came to Ireland from another land with four magnificent capitals. Each capital was led by a master of wisdom rather than a king. One of these cities was Falias. From Falias came the great inauguration stone called the Lia Fail. The oldest accounts name Morfessa as the wisdom master of Falias. She gave the Tuatha De the stone when they sailed for Ireland. The Lia Fail later served as a sacred stone of kingship and inauguration. It marked the power of the rightful ruler who stood upon it.
objective: Document the Irish hero Morfessa and the Lia Fail stone.
key_results: Record Morfessa as the wisdom master whose name means great wisdom.
Record Falias as one of four capitals of the Tuatha De Danann, each led by a wisdom master.
Record the Lia Fail as the inauguration stone Morfessa gave when they sailed for Ireland.
